routes.label: Compare equal-distance travel times using the speed ratio

question: On a trip to the beach, Anh traveled \(50\) miles on the highway and \(10\) miles on a coastal access road. He drove three times as fast on the highway as on the coastal road. If Anh spent \(30\) minutes driving on the coastal road, how many minutes did his entire trip take?
solution:
Compare the time needed to drive the same \(10\)-mile distance on the two roads. On the highway Anh drives three times as fast, so he needs one third as much time: \(30/3=10\) minutes per \(10\) miles.

The \(50\)-mile highway portion therefore takes \(5\cdot10=50\) minutes. Adding the \(30\) minutes on the coastal road gives

\[
50+30=\boxed{80}\text{ minutes},
\]

choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\). Speed and travel time are inversely related when the distance is fixed.
